title: LTS life-cycle schematic and compatibility matrix for inference stack
creator: Asha Patel
description: Produce a single, consumable LTS life-cycle schematic and compatibility matrix that spans runtime, Redwood API, official SDKs, and Console features. The artifact should enable engineering, PM, and support to answer: which versions can co-exist, what upgrade paths are supported, what automated checks the upgrade tooling must run, and which rollout gates are mandatory for each channel. Deliverable: diagram (draw.io), CSV compatibility matrix, and a short playbook for upgrade automation and rollback behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A single compatibility matrix CSV covering runtime binary builds, API contract versions, SDK minor versions, and Console feature flags exists
Compatibility bands (LTS, Stable, Edge) are defined with allowed upgrade/downgrade transitions
Upgrade tooling spec updated: preflight checks, semantic negotiation rules, and migration steps are documented
Rollout gates enumerated and mapped to automation hooks in Console and CI/CD
Stakeholders (runtime, SDK, API, console) have reviewed and provided explicit sign-off
decisions: Adopt compatibility bands instead of strict single-version alignment: LTS (12mo), Stable (3mo), Edge (continuous)
Semantic versioning will be supplemented with a compatibility label (compat:vN) emitted at build time
Downgrades will be allowed only within the same compatibility band and only with explicit operator confirmation
Console will surface per-route supported model/runtime combinations and will block cross-band rollouts by default
timeline: Week 0: draft schematic and gather runtime/SDK version metadata; Week 1: propose matrix and automation hooks; Week 2: cross-team review and iterate; Week 3: finalize CSV + playbook; Week 4: sign-offs and merge specs into docs repo
rollout_gates: Unit + integration test matrix pass for target upgrade path
Performance regression check: p50/p95 token latency within 5% and throughput within 10%
Canary step: 5% traffic for 24h with no SLO violations
Quality monitors: prompt set evals show no drop in top-3 metric beyond threshold
Observability hooks present: tracing, token-cost breakdown, and KV cache hit metrics
upgrade_tools_changes: Add a compatibility-check subcommand to the CLI that consumes the CSV and returns allowed transitions
Implement manifest translator in the control plane to automatically pin SDK adapter versions when runtime moves to a new minor
Migration preflight will validate kernel ABI compatibility and required quantization profiles
Upgrade CLI will support dry-run mode that outputs exact traffic routing changes and canary config
Rollback safety: tooling must snapshot route configs and model pins prior to any rollout
comments: 2025-02-12 - AP: Initial draft uploaded to Confluence and shared with runtime and SDK leads
2025-02-18 - DO: Requested addition of kernel ABI column to CSV; runtime team will provide mapping by 2025-02-21
2025-02-24 - MC: Noted that Console route-level blocking must respect customer Dedicated contracts; added as an exception to the playbook
2025-03-03 - AP: Incorporated perf gate thresholds after discussion with SRE; updated acceptance criteria
risks: Incomplete kernel ABI metadata could lead to failed upgrades in on-prem environments
Edge-only features may be accidentally surfaced to LTS if release branches are not gated
Customer Dedicated contracts may require manual exception handling, increasing operational cost
Automated downgrade without data migration hooks may cause inference artifacts to be incompatible
notes: Coordinate a short cross-team workshop (runtime, SDK, console, SRE, PM) during Week 1 to align on columns required in the CSV. Prefer CSV column names: artifact, semantic_version, compat_label, kernel_abi, api_contract, sdk_adapter, console_flag, supported_transitions. Ensure the CSV can be consumed by the CLI and the control plane manifest translator.
